# JOURNAL — optimizer handover (append-only, whole run)

YOU (the optimizer) own this file. It is the running, accumulating handover across ALL iterations — accepted AND rejected — and it is NEVER reset. Each iteration you APPEND one new entry at the bottom (under the marker line); you do NOT edit or delete earlier entries. Read the whole journal before proposing, so you build on EVERY prior attempt (not just the last accepted one) and never re-test a refuted idea.

You CANNOT know your own gate result while you write — the harness scores you AFTER you stop and stamps a **RESULT** line (outcome + Δ + the tasks you measurably broke/fixed, plus the ones whose move was too small to resolve) right below your entry. So do NOT write 'what worked' as a guess. To learn what actually worked, READ the framework RESULT lines of prior entries (and LEDGER.md): an entry whose RESULT says `rejected` with `broke={...}` tells you which specific edits to drop or redesign — its diff.patch is in ./prior_iterations/<id>/.

Append your entry for THIS iteration below the marker, using this shape (INTENT only — the framework appends the RESULT):

    ## Iteration <your candidate id> — <one-line headline of what you tried>
    - Changes I made (1 line per edit; name the file/tool + cluster it targets):
    - Per change, the EXPECTED effect + why it's safe (which failing task it should fix;
      why no passing task changes behavior):
    - Building on prior RESULTS: which prior entries' broke/fixed I used, and what I
      did NOT re-try because a prior RESULT showed it regressed (cite ids):
    - Refuted hypotheses (a prior RESULT proved this is NOT the fix — never re-test):
    - High-value clusters still NOT cracked (and the guard/tool designs already tried):
    - Plateau signal (are the last few RESULTs flat/negative? if so, which LEVER to switch
      to — e.g. a NEW composite tool instead of another guard, or prompt instead of code):
    - Cost-reduction opportunity (if `cost`/`latency`/`num_messages` is a declared objective,
      run `detect_loop_patterns.py --run-dir $R --tag $BEST --split val` — free, no extra
      eval — and check its `by_tool` map for a same-tool-called-N-times-in-a-row pattern. A
      hit names the exact tool + repeat count: propose a composite/bulk tool (capability
      `tools`), a bundled script entrypoint (`skills-package`), or upfront-batched
      instructions (`prompt`/`system-prompt`) that replace the N calls with one. No hit
      (or cost/latency not a declared objective): say so plainly, do not leave this blank):
    - Focus next iteration:

## Iteration cand_0001 — empty-seed init: payment code-enforcement + DB-safe communicate returns + anti-stall prose
- Changes I made (1 line per edit):
  - tools.py `book_reservation`: per-item payment-dict normalize (`_normalize_payment_dict`: id→payment_id, drop type/source, default amount) — cluster B (`{type,id}` → "payment_id Field required", tasks 8/23/25).
  - tools.py `book_reservation`: payment auto-correct on sum mismatch (single method→total; else single credit card absorbs remainder) + re-sync `payment_history=deepcopy(payment_methods)` after correction — cluster B/C (wrong amounts 8/25; the hashed-field latent bug).
  - tools.py `book_reservation` + `update_reservation_baggages`: deterministic `nonfree` recompute from policy allowance table + `if total_price>0` payment guard — cluster F (defensive no-op; guard kills spurious "payment not found" at $0).
  - tools.py `book`/`update_reservation_flights`/`update_reservation_baggages`/`update_reservation_passengers`/`cancel_reservation`: enriched dict return with `payment_summary` + `communicate_to_user` stating the EXACT $ — cluster C (COMMUNICATE omissions 11/23).
  - tools.py `update_reservation_passengers`: actionable count-mismatch error (names current count, "modify in place") — cluster D (duplicate-passenger strand 17/22).
  - policy.md RULE 1 (confirm-once-then-execute, worked right/wrong examples) — cluster A (7 stall trials); RULE 2 (speak exact $); RULE 3 (baggage table); RULE 4 (payment sums); RULE 5 (disambiguate reservation by route, do eligible part / transfer only impossible, modify passengers in place) — clusters C/D/E; RULE 6 softness clause.
- Per change, EXPECTED effect + why safe: payment normalize/auto-correct make the wrong-amount/wrong-format book attempts succeed on first try with the SAME final DB the flaky retries reached (verified T8=$348, T25=[gc128,cc247], live DB) — fires ONLY on mismatch so a correct booking is a verified no-op. Enriched returns are DB-safe (tau2 hashes only self.db; returns pass through to_json_str) and hand the exact figure (T11 refund $5244) to the reader for COMMUNICATE. Baggage recompute = policy arithmetic = gold value when total is right, no-op otherwise. Prose rules general, traced to policy; softness clause prevents over-compliance.
- Building on prior RESULTS: none exist (first iteration). Re-validated every lever from auto-memory `tau2-airline-reward-mechanics` against current tau2 source before shipping.
- Refuted hypotheses: none yet.
- High-value clusters still NOT cracked: A (stall/USER_STOP) only prose-mitigated — if it persists, next lever is to investigate whether the write can be made to execute in the same turn as confirmation (user-sim-driven, no tool lever). D (wrong reservation 17/22) relies on prose + error; a code disambiguation tool (e.g. `find_reservation_by_route`) is the untried design.
- Plateau signal: n/a (iteration 1).
- Cost-reduction: cost/latency/num_messages not declared objectives for this run (objective = DB×COMMUNICATE reward). `detect_loop_patterns.py` not run. The error→retry loops (wrong payment amount, re-ask confirmation) are nonetheless reduced as a side effect of the payment auto-correct/normalize.
- Focus next iteration: measure which clusters moved; if A dominates residual loss, pursue the same-turn-execute design; if D/E remain, consider a route→reservation resolver tool and a composite "do eligible writes" path.

> **RESULT (framework, measured):** ACCEPTED (new champion) · val=0.467 Δ=+0.133 · fixed={—} · broke={—} · unresolved={11, 12, 19, 23, 25, 37, 40, 8} (moved less than 2·SE of its own measurement — NOT evidence the edit touched those tasks; do not redesign on them).
<!-- cand_0001: ACCEPTED val=0.467 Δ=+0.133 -->

## Iteration cand_0002 — kill the confirm-then-STOP stall (decisive execution) + basic-economy cabin-upgrade knowledge + atomic modify_reservation
- Changes I made (1 line per edit; file/tool + cluster):
  - policy.md RULE 1 REWRITTEN → decision chain: once every required detail is in hand, the turn MUST end in the WRITE tool call, never a standalone "Shall I proceed?" question; worked right/wrong examples — cluster A (stall).
  - policy.md base confirmation line (line 7) reconciled to point at RULE 1 (removes the stacked contradiction with "must obtain explicit confirmation") — cluster A.
  - policy.md RULE 5 +bullet: a cabin change IS allowed on basic economy (flights-vs-cabin distinction) — cluster B (task 22 always-fail, 17).
  - policy.md RULE 5 +bullets: never transfer over a number you're unsure of (trust the tool's returned figure); finish every write of a multi-part request — cluster C (over-transfer).
  - tools.py NEW composite `modify_reservation(reservation_id, payment_id, cabin?, flights?, passengers?, total_baggages?)` — applies cabin/flights + passengers + baggages atomically in ONE call, reuses existing flights for a cabin-only change, returns the exact net charge/refund — cluster D (17/22 multi-write) + A (fewer confirm points). Primitives kept (additive).
- EXPECTED effect + why safe: E1 converts the 4 clear stall trials (8/12/19/40 t0) and helps every multi-write task by making the agent execute instead of yielding — SAFE because it is literally the behavior of the passing trials (11/37, 40 t1/t2) which execute directly; no passing task relied on a separate confirm turn. E3 reverses task 22's wrong refusal (verified policy allows basic-economy cabin change). E5 verified on the LIVE DB: FQ8APE → economy + Omar Rossi + 3 bags = $209 atomic; GV1N64 cabin-only downgrade = $5244 refund (== task 11 gold, so routing 11 through it is a no-op); count-mismatch error propagates; $0 baggage path clean. Additive tool (15 total) so selection on passing tasks is preserved.
- Building on prior RESULTS: cand_0001 ACCEPTED (val 0.467) with everything `unresolved` (<2·SE) — no task has a measured break/fix, so nothing to avoid re-introducing. I PRESERVED all of cand_0001's verified code levers (payment normalize/auto-correct, payment_history re-sync, baggage recompute, enriched returns) and did not touch them.
- Refuted hypotheses: none measured yet (only one prior RESULT, all unresolved).
- High-value clusters still NOT cracked: the stall (A) can only be mitigated, not code-forced — the model chooses whether to emit a tool call. If A persists after this prose+structural push, the remaining lever is removing the update_* primitives so `modify_reservation` is the only modify path (deferred — regression risk on passing 11/37/40). Task 25 (max_steps search loop; user ###OUT-OF-SCOPE###) is likely partly infra noise.
- Plateau signal: n/a (2nd iteration; parent was an accept). If cand_0002 is rejected, the most likely culprit is E1 over-rotating the model into premature writes — in that case keep E3 (knowledge) + E5 (tool) and re-tune E1 to a softer "execute once the user confirms in-turn" wording.
- Cost-reduction: cost/latency/num_messages not declared objectives (objective = DB×COMMUNICATE). `detect_loop_patterns.py` not run. `modify_reservation` nonetheless collapses 3 write round-trips into 1 for multi-part modifications as a side benefit.
- Focus next iteration: read the RESULT. If A moved, consider the primitive-removal step for `modify_reservation`. If B/C fixed task 22/17, look next at the remaining flaky booking tasks (8/23/25) for the certificate/multi-card split path.

> **RESULT (framework, measured):** ACCEPTED (new champion) · val=0.567 Δ=+0.100 · fixed={—} · broke={—} · unresolved={11, 17, 22, 23, 25, 40} (moved less than 2·SE of its own measurement — NOT evidence the edit touched those tasks; do not redesign on them).

## Iteration cand_0003 — post-stall residual: dup/compounding writes + cancel-vs-modify-vs-transfer + grab-first-reservation resolver
- Changes I made (1 line per edit; file/tool + cluster):
  - tools.py NEW `find_reservation(user_id, origin?, destination?)` — one call returns a compact summary of ALL the user's reservations (id/route/dates/cabin/pax/status + match flag) — cluster C (17/22 modified the WRONG reservation, grabbing the first id without matching the route).
  - tools.py `book_reservation` in-body duplicate guard — if an ACTIVE reservation already matches same origin/destination/flight_type/passenger-set/travel-dates, raise an actionable error naming it and saying to MODIFY instead — cluster A (8 double-book; defends 23-style re-book).
  - policy.md RULE 6 (new) "one decision, ONE write per reservation; never a corrected second write" + WRONG/CORRECT worked examples — cluster A (12 modify twice, 8 book twice, 23 book 3×).
  - policy.md RULE 7 (new) a cabin/flight/baggage change is a MODIFICATION — never cancel-and-rebook, never split one trip into several reservations to apply more certificates / lower a card charge; downgrade+refund = cabin modification not cancel — cluster B (23 always-fail cancel+split; 11 cancelled instead of modifying).
  - policy.md RULE 5 (+bullet) check ALL four cancel-eligibility conditions before transferring/refusing a cancellation; transfer only when no write tool can satisfy — cluster B (19 transferred instead of cancelling).
  - policy.md RULE 5 disambiguation bullet rewritten to call `find_reservation` first and match by route; renumbered old RULE 6 softness → RULE 8 — cluster C.
- Per change, EXPECTED effect + why safe: E1 surfaces all candidates so the mid reader stops acting on the first id (verified live: FQ8APE flagged as the EWR→ORD match, UM3OG5 not) — additive READ, passing tasks unaffected. E2 kills the doubled-reservation DB corruption (verified: 2nd identical-trip book blocked even with a different flight number; task 25's same-route/same-dates but DIFFERENT-passenger-count booking is NOT blocked → no false positive; fresh booking OK). E3/E4/E7 are general prose tightenings traced to policy (max 1 cert/reservation; cancel conditions), with worked examples for the mid reader; they tighten decisions, never loosen a passing one, so no passing trial changes.
- Building on prior RESULTS: cand_0001 + cand_0002 both ACCEPTED with every task `unresolved` (<2·SE) — no measured break/fix, so nothing to avoid re-introducing. I PRESERVED all prior verified levers (payment normalize/auto-correct, payment_history re-sync, baggage recompute, enriched returns, RULE 1 anti-stall decision chain, `modify_reservation`) and did not touch them. The stall (cluster A of cand_0002) is no longer the dominant failure in these traces — passing trials now execute the write directly — so I shifted lever to the write-COUNT / write-CHOICE / target-RESERVATION errors that remain.
- Refuted hypotheses: none measured (both prior RESULTs were accepts with all-unresolved; no prior edit was disproven).
- High-value clusters still NOT cracked: task 23 (adversarial cancel+split) is attacked only by prose RULE 7 — if it persists, the untried lever is a code guard in `book_reservation` that refuses creating a NEW reservation for a subset of passengers who were just on a cancelled reservation of the same route this session (session-state anti-split), but that is intricate and risky. Task 8's non-cheapest flight selection is a reasoning error with no clean general fix. Task 12's compounding modify is only prose-mitigated (idempotent snapshot-restore judged too corruption-prone).

# FRAMEWORK-IMPROVEMENTS — suggestions for cap-evolve itself (cross-run)

NOT about this capability or this run's result — about what cap-evolve the FRAMEWORK should change so FUTURE runs (any capability, any project) go better: a confusing prompt section, a missing tool, a file you wished existed, a gate that felt wrong. Optional most iterations; add an entry whenever something about the framework itself (not the task) got in your way or surprised you.

## From cand_0003 (tau2-airline smoke run)
- **The all-unresolved RESULT is near-uninformative for steering.** Every RESULT so far
  stamps `fixed={—} broke={—}` with ALL tasks `unresolved` (per-task move < 2·SE), even
  across a clear +0.133 then +0.100 aggregate climb. The optimizer is told "the whole
  thing went up" but never "which edit did it," so each iteration must re-diagnose from
  trajectories to know what worked. SUGGESTION: when per-task significance can't be
  reached at the current trial count, the framework could report a cheaper aggregate
  attribution signal — e.g. per-cluster or per-tool deltas, or a note that more trials
  would be needed to resolve a task — rather than a flat `unresolved` set the optimizer
  is explicitly warned not to act on. Right now the richest signal lives in the raw
  trajectories, which the optimizer has to re-cluster by hand every iteration.
- **A 3-iteration budget with a per-task 2·SE gate means no edit can ever be individually
  validated within a run.** The gate protects against regressions (good) but the
  optimizer never gets a confirmed "this lever fixed task X" within the budget, so
  INSIGHTS "what worked" stays hypothesis-level. SUGGESTION: either raise val trial count
  on the final iteration for a cleaner read, or expose a cheap per-edit ablation hook so
  a shipped candidate's individual edits can be credited post-hoc.
- **Stale cross-iteration summary risk.** The compaction summary carried a wrong
  diagnosis ("omitted cabin upgrade" for 17/22) that was only caught by re-reading the
  live tool-call targets. A short framework note in the task preamble — "re-derive the
  cluster map from the current champion's trajectories; do not trust a prior summary's
  diagnosis" — would harden every run against inherited mis-diagnosis.

# PROCESS — cand_0003 (parent cand_0002, val 0.567)

Reward model: **DB × COMMUNICATE** (product; either 0 ⇒ task 0). Tool RETURN values are
NOT hashed — only `self.db`. Diagnosed THIS iteration's `./trajectories/` (30 val trials
of cand_0002) by reading the actual traces, not the stale summary. The confirm-then-STOP
stall that dominated cand_0002's diagnosis is now largely gone (passing trials execute
the write directly). The residual loss is three DECISION/BEHAVIORAL patterns the mid
reader still gets wrong on some trials. I verified each code edit on the LIVE airline DB
with the edited `AirlineTools` (run venv).

## Ranked cluster list (leverage = # failing trials × score recoverable)

| rank | cluster | tasks (trials) | root cause | tag | lever |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| A | **Duplicated / compounding WRITE** | 23 t0/t1/t2 (ALWAYS-fail), 12 t0/t2, 8 t0/t1 | Agent writes, then re-writes to "correct" it. The first write is not undone: `book_reservation` makes a NEW reservation and each write appends a charge, so a corrective repeat STACKS → doubled DB → 0. 23 cancels then books 3×; 12 modifies business then economy; 8 books twice (different flight). | BEHAVIORAL | code: duplicate-booking guard in `book_reservation`; prose RULE 6 "one decision, one write" |
| B | **Cancel/split vs modify; over-transfer** | 23 t0/t1/t2, 11 t1, 19 t0/t1 | Wrong write-action choice. 23: user pressures agent to cancel + split one party into 3 reservations to use 3 certificates (policy forbids >1 cert/reservation). 11: "downgrade + refund difference" done as a full CANCEL instead of a cabin modification. 19: agent TRANSFERS instead of cancelling, having checked only the insurance condition and not the other three cancel-eligibility conditions. | DECISION | prose RULE 7 (cabin change = modify, never cancel-and-rebook / split to game payments) + RULE 5 cancel-eligibility check |
| C | **Wrong reservation targeted (grab-first-id)** | 17 t1, 22 t0/t1 | User names the trip by route ("New York to Chicago"), gives no id. Agent fetches the FIRST reservation id and acts on it (SEA→DFW `UM3OG5`) without confirming the route, instead of the matching `FQ8APE` (EWR→ORD, basic economy). Passing trials fetch several candidates and match. | CAPABILITY-GAP | code: new `find_reservation(user_id)` resolver returning a compact summary of ALL reservations in one call; RULE 5 points at it |

A+B overlap on the always-failing task 23 (3 trials, full recoverable) — the biggest
single leverage — and together cover every failing trial except the flight-selection
noise in 8 (wrong cheapest flight, a reasoning error no capability edit fixes cleanly).

## Edits made this iteration

| id | edit | file / surface | class (SKILL lever) | targets | protects passing? |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| E1 | New READ tool `find_reservation(user_id, origin?, destination?)` — loops the user's reservations, returns compact {id, origin, destination, flight_type, cabin, dates, num_passengers, status, matches_filter} so all candidates are visible in ONE call | tools.py | code: loop/resolver tool (lever 5) + literal per-param docs for the mid reader | C (17, 22) | yes — additive READ; passing tasks already resolve correctly |
| E2 | Duplicate-booking guard in `book_reservation`: before creating, scan the user's ACTIVE reservations; if one matches same origin/destination/flight_type/passenger-set/travel-dates, raise an actionable error naming the existing id and telling the agent to MODIFY it | tools.py | code: in-body guard (lever 1) | A (8; defends 23-style re-book) | yes — verified task 25 (same route/dates, DIFFERENT passenger count) does NOT fire |
| E3 | RULE 6 (new): "one decision, ONE write per reservation; never issue a corrected second write" with WRONG/CORRECT worked examples | policy.md | prose (add rule + reason + example) | A (12, 8, 23) | yes — passing trials already write once |
| E4 | RULE 7 (new): a cabin/flight/baggage change is a MODIFICATION — never cancel-and-rebook; never split one trip into several reservations to apply more certificates / lower a card charge; downgrade+refund = cabin modification, not cancel | policy.md | prose (add sourced decision rule + example) | B (23, 11) | yes — tightens, never loosens a passing decision |
| E5 | RULE 5: cancel-eligibility check — verify ALL four conditions (24h / airline-cancelled / business / insurance+covered) before transferring or refusing a cancellation; transfer only when no write tool can satisfy the request | policy.md | prose (tighten decision rule, traced to Cancel-flight policy) | B (19) | yes — states policy exactly, adds no new permission |
| E6 | RULE 5 disambiguation bullet rewritten to call `find_reservation` first and match by route/dates; "do not act on the first id you see" | policy.md | prose (rewrite + point at new tool) | C (17, 22) | yes |

## Verify-the-fix (ran against the LIVE airline DB with the edited AirlineTools, run venv)

- **Registration**: edited toolset imports and tau2 `get_tools()` returns **16** tools
  incl. `find_reservation` (< ~20 limit). No registration break.
- **E1 fires on C**: `find_reservation('omar_rossi_1241', origin='EWR', destination='ORD')`
  returns all 4 reservations and flags **FQ8APE** (EWR→ORD, basic_economy, 1 pax)
  `matches_filter=True`, the exact reservation the failing trials missed; `UM3OG5`
  (SEA→DFW, the one they wrongly grabbed) is `False`.
- **E2 fires on A, not on passing**: 1st book of a trip succeeds; an identical-trip 2nd
  book (same pax/route/dates, even a different flight number — the task-8 pattern) is
  BLOCKED with the actionable error. Task 25 (ivan_muller_7015 books DTW→SEA 1 pax while
  existing G72NSF is DTW→SEA **2 pax**) passes the guard — the passenger-set differs, so
  no false positive. A fresh unrelated booking succeeds.
- **E3–E6 (prose)**: each is general (no task id/answer), traces to the policy, and
  tightens (never loosens) a decision; renumbering RULE 6→RULE 8 kept every constraint.

## What I deliberately SKIPPED and why
- **Making `modify_reservation` idempotent (snapshot-restore) for task 12**: the only
  clean code fix would restore the pre-session reservation + user balances + seat
  availability before re-applying — too much state to restore correctly, high corruption
  risk. Handled task 12 with RULE 6 prose instead (no passing trial calls modify twice,
  so prose + the atomic tool suffice).
- **Removing the `update_*` primitives so `modify_reservation` is the only path** (the
  structural lever flagged in JOURNAL): passing 40 t2 and 12 t1 call `update_*` directly,
  and `modify_reservation` requires a `payment_id` even for free passenger-only changes —
  removal would strand those. Regression risk > upside; left additive.
- **Task 8 flight selection** (agent picks a non-cheapest flight): a reasoning error, not
  a capability gap; no general code/prose edit fixes it without hardcoding.

## Subagents / parallelism
Diagnosed directly (traces are compact JSON; a single pass over all 30 trials + targeted
live-DB checks was faster and more reliable than fan-out round-trips). No subagents used.
